subject: difference observed covariance matrix with cov() and inspect(fit,"sampstat")?

messages.author: 598408fcf0cedf99
messages.subject: difference observed covariance matrix with cov() and inspect(fit,"sampstat")?
parts:
Dear all,

I noticed that when I manually calculate the observed covariance matrix by applying cov() to my data set, the resulting numbers are always somewhat different from what I get after fitting a SEM and using inspect(fit,"sampstat").

First I thought it was because I had missing values, but even with a complete data set and a SEM without latent variables, there is still a difference.
If anyone could explain to me why this is, and if they are supposed to be different, which one is better to report, I'd be most grateful.

Thanks!
M.

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: difference observed covariance matrix with cov() and inspect(fit,"sampstat")?
parts:
> If anyone could explain to me why this is, and if they are supposed to
> be different, which one is better to report, I'd be most grateful.

When estimator = "ML" (and friends), and likelihood = "normal" (the
default), then sample.cov.rescale = TRUE by default.

The cov() function divides the elements by N-1, while the ML estimate
divides the elements by N. So the user-supplied covariance matrix is
'rescaled' so that the elements are divided by N.

You can switch this if by using the sample.cov.rescale = FALSE argument.

Yves.

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: difference observed covariance matrix with cov() and inspect(fit,"sampstat")?
parts:
On 12/08/2016 10:36 AM, M. wrote:
> Yves, see an example below.
> Unless I am missing something obvious here, the sample.cov.rescale
> option has no influence on the covariance matrix returned by inspect()...

I (incorrectly) presumed that you were providing the sample covariance
matrix directly, using the sample.cov= argument. Only then will the
sample.cov.rescale argument have an effect.

If you provide full data, you need to change the likelihood argument:

fit1 <- sem(mod, data=dat,estimator="ML",likelihood="wishart")
> Also, what is the rationale behind the default rescaling of the matrix?

The estimator. Maximum likelihood requires 'N'. While the (traditional)
wishart approach requires 'N-1'.

Yves.

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: difference observed covariance matrix with cov() and inspect(fit,"sampstat")?
parts:
On 12/08/2016 01:41 PM, M. wrote:
> On a more practical note: I'm asked to provide the observed
> variance-covariance matrix of a SEM for a publication. Would it make
> sense to provide the rescaled matrix, as that is the one used in my SEM,
> or would you rather provide the "raw" sample variance-covariance matrix?

It does not matter, as long as you clearly say if the elements (in the
table) were divided by N or N-1.

> Finally, what are the advantages of "normal" over "Wishart" likelihood
> (if any)?

The 'old' approach is the wishart approach. But this only works if data
is complete. If data is missing, we need to switch to the normal
approach. For consistency reasons, it seems better to stick to the
normal approach in both cases. The actual differences are rather small
and are only visible when N is small.

Yves.

messages.subject: Re: difference observed covariance matrix with cov() and inspect(fit,"sampstat")?
parts: > > fit1 <- sem(mod, data=dat,estimator="ML",likelihood="wishart")

By default, lavaan will use listwise deletion. To use the 'ml' approach,
you need to specify:

fit1 <- sem(mod, data=dat,estimator="ML", missing="ml")

Yves.
